Every now and again, a grand residence from an earlier era comes to market, seeking a new steward to carry its history forward. This impressive Queen Anne Victorian home on historic Sumner Hill yearns for restoration. Twelve gracious rooms offer artisan-crafted woodwork & period details throughout. A dramatic entry foyer features ornate wood-framed arches, a fireplace with an elaborate mantel and lift-top bench, tall wainscoting, stained glass, and a sweeping staircase. Beyond, double parlors showcase pocket doors, bay windows, a petite plant solarium, fireplaces in each room, and inlaid oak floors. Off the kitchen, the formal dining room boasts a built-in sideboard, another fireplace, and direct access to the rear deck. Sleeping quarters above comprise six bedrooms with wood flooring, some highlighted by bay windows and fireplaces, along with two full baths, and a generously sized primary bedroom with charming covered porch and balcony. Additional features include original decorative windows, abundant built-ins, a unique linen room with a wall of cabinetry and a cedar closet on an upper floor, and remnants of the original scullery on the lower level. The grounds hold the promise of a lovely yard and gardens. The western side of the house fronts on a private way, creating off-street parking among an intimate enclave of neighboring homes. Sumner Hill is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Once part of a vast tract of land known as the Greenough Estate, the property was subdivided in the late 1800's. A cluster of architecturally significant homes was built throughout the hill at that time, many owned by prominent figures who helped shape Boston's economic and social landscape. Today, Sumner Hill remains highly sought-after for its beautifully restored residences and proximity to Jamaica Plain's cultural and natural treasures, along with its many notable restaurants and shops. Come make this your dream home!

A Rare Once In A Lifetime Riverfront Legacy A truly extraordinary property, a magnificent French Colonial estate inspired by the celebrated Louisiana architect A. Hays Town. Set on expansive, beautifully landscaped grounds beneath majestic oak trees, this exceptional residence blends timeless Louisiana architecture with the serenity and beauty of its riverfront setting. A. Hays Town is one of Louisiana's most influential residential architects. A Tulane trained architect, Town became renowned for creating a distinctive regional style that drew from Louisiana's French, Spanish and Creole architectural heritage. His homes were celebrated for their use of French doors, shutters, exposed beams, brick and stone floors, pigeoneers, natural materials and a thoughtful relationship between the house, gardens and surrounding landscape. His work helped shape the look of modern Louisiana residential architecture and continues to influence homes throughout the state. That spirit is beautifully reflected in this custom built 1995 residence. Designed with extraordinary attention to detail, the home possesses the character and warmth of a timeless Louisiana estate while offering the comforts of a thoughtfully designed modern home. Gorgeous French doors and shutters surround the property, while exposed beams and stone flooring bring texture and authenticity to the interiors. Custom paint colors by award winning designer Louis Aubert add another layer of sophistication. The first floor primary suite offers convenience and privacy, complemented by a dedicated office and gracious living spaces that open toward the spectacular grounds. A new kitchen featuring marble counter tops adds modern functionality while remaining beautifully in keeping with the home's classic French Colonial character. The approach to the property is nothing short of dramatic, with a long circular driveway leading through the magnificent grounds to the residence. Lovingly cared for by the same family since 1995

Some houses can't be built again. 170 Halsey Street is an 1880s Neo-Grec brownstone in the landmarked Bedford Historic District, between Marcy and Tompkins Avenues, and it has kept the craftsmanship of its era almost entirely intact. A high stoop with original cast-iron railings and newels rises to a facade with a two-story angled bay, fan-carved lintels and a bracketed cornice. Inside, the original staircase climbs all four floors, with its carved newel post, wood banister and turned balusters. The parlor floor has ornate plaster ceiling medallions, tray ceilings, crown moldings and picture rails. Pocket doors and double doors sit under incised, dentil-trimmed Eastlake crowns, and a towering carved walnut pier mirror anchors the parlor. The bedroom floor has two generous bedrooms joined by original washstand closets in the shared wall. The plumbing is already in place, which makes them a natural starting point for a primary suite with its own bath. The top floor has full-height bedrooms on one side and a space under the pitched roofline on the other that would suit a library, studio or office. Four original mantels with ornate cast-iron covers are spread through the house, along with built-in wardrobes under carved arches and sunny bay windows. The garden level has a formal dining room with a mantel and an eat-in kitchen that opens onto a deep, private, fenced garden with mature trees. A full cellar provides storage. On a 20 * 100 ft lot, the house could be restored as a grand single-family residence or laid out in a flexible configuration, with modern kitchens, baths and systems added alongside details that are rarely found today. The house is about 4-minutes to the A/C express at Nostrand Avenue, and the cafes and shops of Tompkins Avenue and Fulton Street are close by.

Some houses can't be built again. 170 Halsey Street is an 1880s Neo-Grec brownstone in the landmarked Bedford Historic District, between Marcy and Tompkins Avenues, and it has kept the craftsmanship of its era almost entirely intact. A high stoop with original cast-iron railings and newels rises to a facade with a two-story angled bay, fan-carved lintels and a bracketed cornice. Inside, the original staircase climbs all four floors, with its carved newel post, wood banister and turned balusters. The parlor floor has ornate plaster ceiling medallions, tray ceilings, crown moldings and picture rails. Pocket doors and double doors sit under incised, dentil-trimmed Eastlake crowns, and a towering carved walnut pier mirror anchors the parlor. The bedroom floor has two generous bedrooms joined by original washstand closets in the shared wall. The plumbing is already in place, which makes them a natural starting point for a primary suite with its own bath. The top floor has full-height bedrooms on one side and a space under the pitched roofline on the other that would suit a library, studio or office. Four original mantels with ornate cast-iron covers are spread through the house, along with built-in wardrobes under carved arches and sunny bay windows. The garden level has a formal dining room with a mantel and an eat-in kitchen that opens onto a deep, private, fenced garden with mature trees. A full cellar provides storage. On a 20 * 100 ft lot, the house could be restored as a grand single-family residence or laid out in a flexible configuration, with modern kitchens, baths and systems added alongside details that are rarely found today. The house is about 4-minutes to the A/C express at Nostrand Avenue, and the cafes and shops of Tompkins Avenue and Fulton Street are close by.

Tucked away on a quiet dead-end street, this beautifully updated 3-bedroom, 2-bath home offers an exceptional blend of privacy, comfort, and convenience on a generous 8,500-square-foot lot. Space, versatility, and a sought-after Queen Anne setting come together in this home near the conveniences of Queen Anne and Fremont. Come see this house today!

First time on the market in 60 years! Sited on a quiet residential street in the coveted Admiral district, this 1926, 3340 SQFT Craftsman is ready for your creativity and vision. Flooded with natural light and rich with vintage charm, the main level circular floor plan lives large. Upon entry, one is struck by the spaciousness of the living and formal dining room, oak hardwood floors, coved ceilings, traditional millwork, and fireplace. Best of all you are only 2 blocks from all that vibrant California Avenue has to offer; putting schools, parks, coffee houses, restaurants, local markets, boutique shops and the Junction's Sunday Farmer's market within minutes of your home. Enjoy a Walk Score of 87.

text: Experience the perfect blend of modern luxury and Pacific Northwest style in this stunning 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom Maple Leaf home.
